scope: Proposition 6.1 (Cone criterion) of the manuscript “A Torsion-Free Group Algebra That Is Not Directly Finite” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Group-Algebra-That-Is-Not-Directly-Finite-October-4-2026/direct-finiteness.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 197 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7950476863f21811), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 24-25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Γ = ΓA ⊔ ΓB be a finite graph immersed in the rose F, with chosen roots xA, xB, and let X and G be defined by (2.1). If Γ admits no reduced spherical 24 arrangement as in Definition 5.1, then π2(X) = 0 and the root-protection condition (2.4) holds. Moreover, X is a finite aspherical complex of dimension at most two, and G is finitely presented and torsion-free.
